review_notes: Read hash-bound handoff, proposal and functionality document; empty proposal reconciles with explicit retention rather than equivalent rewrites. Independently inspected canonical and rendered AXCL lines 1-142. Source supports all indicated section-layout deferrals and rejects demonstrated atomicity; no overrides needed. Inherited supported function knowledge and relationships remain retained, without certifying compiled section mapping.
unresolved: Compiled .bss/.sbss membership, sizes and actual alignment remain unverified; source assertions specify requirements only.
Buffer-rotation relationship is supported but its baseline atomicity rationale remains unsupported and deferred.
Invalid-mode assertion behavior across build configurations and DSP consumption of HRTF history remain unestablished.

contradictions.reason: Accepted deferral of both .bss facts and both .bss links: canonical source declares command-list buffers and a separate HRTF-history array. The buffers' dimensions, payload role and alternation are supported, but equating the entire compiled section with those buffers, or asserting its exact size and actual alignment, requires compiled evidence. Initialization alignment assertions do not establish placement.

Accepted deferral of both .sbss facts and both .sbss links: the mode, position, cursor and cycle-estimate declarations and their logical roles are supported. Source does not establish their exhaustive membership, order or claimed 16-byte grouping in the compiled small-BSS section.

Accepted deferral of link:782b1fdb-9597-4274-a5a9-dd1e914316ad's atomicity rationale. Capturing the current address, incrementing and masking the index, and redirecting the writer establish double-buffer rotation through ordinary sequential assignments, not an atomic handoff guarantee. The functionality document correctly preserves that distinction; the relationship itself remains supported.
